welcome.title: Getting started: check {product} works for you
welcome.body:
{product} is connected. Four steps, about five minutes:

1. Ask your AI: "Which of my machines can you reach?" It calls `machines` and lists each machine and whether it is online.
2. On your phone, open {hub}/approvals. Tap **Notify this phone**, then **Send me a test approval**. Approve it from the notification.
3. Ask your AI for something small on one machine, for example: "Show me the free disk space on <machine>." Anything you should sign off on waits for you on your phone.
4. Tell your AI it worked, and ask it to close this ticket.

Stuck on a step? Tell your AI which one; it can read this ticket.

operator.title: Operator
operator.account_link: You run this hub: let people in and set their plans on the [operator page](/operator).
operator.status_open: Sign-up is **open**: everyone who connects is let in at once.
operator.status_early_access: Sign-up is **early access**: everyone who connects waits here until you let them in.
operator.how_to_change: To change it, set `early_access.mode` in the site's `site.json` to `open` or `early_access`, then run `hub-up.sh --site DIR --site-only`. Once it is open, people waiting are let in on their next request; nobody already in is ever put back.

operator.not_from_here: That came from another site, so nothing was changed. Use the operator page itself.
operator.admitted_empty: Nobody has been let in yet.

analytics.title: Analytics
analytics.operator_link: How people find and use this hub: [analytics](/operator/analytics).
analytics.intro: Counted by this hub itself, as it serves its pages: no cookie, no script, nothing third-party. A visitor counts once a day, so the same person on two days counts twice.
analytics.off: This hub counts nothing: `analytics.enabled` is false in its config (or `DEVAGOTCHI_HUB_ANALYTICS=off`).
analytics.kept: Raw visits are kept {days} days; the daily totals are kept.
analytics.dropped: {n} records were not kept because the hub's queue was full.
analytics.chart_title: Visitors and page views per day
analytics.chart_summary: {views} page views and {visitors} visitors over {n} days.
analytics.funnel_intro: Visitors over these {n} days, and the accounts made in them: how far each got so far.
analytics.active: Active, with a command run: **{week}** in the last 7 days, **{month}** in the last 30.

workflow.finished: All done. Go back to your AI: it carries on from here.
workflow.keep_text: Your AI made this account for you when you connected it, and nothing signs you in to it yet. Add a sign-in now to keep it and see your machines from anywhere. Optional: everything above works without it.
workflow.keep_done: Your account is kept: sign in from anywhere with what you just added.
workflow.command_note: Paste it on that machine as is. It works once, for 15 minutes; pressing the button again gives a new one and the old one stops working.
workflow.name_label: Its name (lowercase letters, digits and dashes)

os_hint.docker: Paste it into a terminal on a Linux machine with Docker Compose and press Enter.
os_hint.host: Paste it into a root shell on the Proxmox or Incus host itself (not inside a guest) and press Enter.
os_hint.linux: Paste it into a terminal on the machine and press Enter; sudo may ask for your password.
os_hint.windows: Open PowerShell (Start, type PowerShell, Enter), paste it and press Enter. No administrator needed.

workflow.no_downloads: This hub hands out no builds, so it has no one-line install to give. Its operator can turn that on.

claude.name: Claude
claude.how: **On claude.ai or in the Claude desktop app:** open **Customize**, then **Connectors**, press **Add custom connector**, paste the address below, press **Add**, then **Connect** on it. **In Claude Code:** run the command below in a terminal, start `claude`, type `/mcp`, choose it and press **Authenticate**. The Free plan holds one custom connector.

chatgpt.name: ChatGPT
chatgpt.how: **In ChatGPT on the web** (Plus, Pro, Business, Enterprise or Education): open **Settings**, then **Apps**, turn on **Developer mode** under **Advanced settings**, press **Create app**, paste the address below as its MCP server, choose **OAuth**, and connect. **In Codex:** run the command below; it opens the sign-in itself.

grok.name: Grok
grok.how: **On grok.com:** open [grok.com/connectors](https://grok.com/connectors), press **New Connector**, choose **Custom**, paste the address below and finish its sign-in. On a Business or Enterprise team, an admin adds the connector first.

cursor.name: Cursor
cursor.how: **In Cursor:** add the entry below to `~/.cursor/mcp.json` (every project) or `.cursor/mcp.json` (this project), save, and press **Connect** next to it under **MCP** when Cursor asks you to sign in.

workflow.client_secured: {client} opens a page to connect: sign in there as you usually do, then press **Connect**.

catalog.description: Define available capabilities, risk explanations, and setup choices for this environment. Access is granted separately.
catalog.confirm_default_help: To select or edit a default that allows full access, unsandboxed operations or unrestricted desktop input, type its exact ID here. The environment-wide unsandboxed policy must also be enabled. Choosing a default does not approve access requests.
catalog.id_help: Use a unique ID with letters, numbers, dots, colons, hyphens, or underscores. It stays fixed after creation.
catalog.structured_help: Enter JSON. Lists use square brackets, for example ["first", "second"].
catalog.remove_help: Removal is refused while another record uses this one. Choose another default before removing a default preset.

projects.title: Manage projects
projects.description: Create a project, change its name or workflow, or remove an empty project. Removed projects keep their history.
projects.name: Project name
projects.id_help: Use lowercase letters, numbers and hyphens. This address stays the same when you rename the project.
projects.remove_help: Projects containing tasks cannot be removed, including completed tasks. Revoke keys restricted to this project first. A shared workflow must be deleted before its original project can be removed. Project history remains available after removal.
projects.retired_notice: This project was removed. Its history is read-only.

configuration.title: Board settings
configuration.description: Choose how this board assigns work, handles time limits, and moves tasks through each stage.
configuration.workflow_help: Changes apply to this board. A state used by a task must keep its key and type; you can change its display name.
configuration.states_help: States describe where a task is. Active work is held by a worker; completed work satisfies dependencies.
configuration.stages_help: Claiming moves a task from waiting to active. Completing moves it forward. Releasing, handing off, or expiring returns it to unfinished work.
configuration.transitions_help: Choose which moves a person can make when a task is not held by a worker.
configuration.heartbeat_help: Workers check in at least this often. Short leases use an earlier check-in, at a third of their length.
configuration.note_kinds_help: Separate lowercase types with commas, for example note, blocker, decision. Leave empty to allow any type. Automatic work and review records are always kept.
configuration.lease_help: A lease reserves a task for one worker. The worker renews it while working. Minimum must be at most default, and default at most maximum.
configuration.expiry_help: Repeatedly expired tasks move to the attention state. Use 0 for no automatic escalation.
configuration.wip_limit: Active tasks per worker on this board
configuration.wip_help: The default work limit for a worker. Use 0 for no limit. A worker-specific limit, when configured, takes precedence.
configuration.priority_help: Lower numbers are picked first when choosing the next task.
configuration.priority_labels_help: One name per line, starting at priority 0. These names appear on tasks; the numeric order stays the same. Leave empty to show P0, P1 and so on.
configuration.environment_help: Separate lowercase names with commas, for example dev, staging, prod. Tasks can name one of these environments.
configuration.distinct: Require a different worker from the previous stage
configuration.saved: Saved. New rules apply to the next request.
configuration.draft: Unsaved changes. Review the form, then save when you are ready.
configuration.conflict: Someone changed this configuration while you were editing. Your draft is shown below. Copy anything you want to keep, then reload the current settings before editing again.
configuration.invalid_form: Check the fields. Durations accept up to three decimal places; limits and priorities must be whole numbers. Each workflow row needs all its fields, with at most 512 rows per section.
configuration.read_only: Only a board owner or administrator can change its settings.
configuration.shared_help: Use one workflow across boards you own. Editing it updates every board using it. Your other boards keep their own rules until you choose a shared workflow.
configuration.shared_authority: Shared workflows require ownership of all boards in this account. A grant to manage one shared project is not enough.
configuration.shared_missing: This shared workflow is no longer available in your account.
configuration.shared_unknown: Unavailable; reload when the hub can read the catalog.
configuration.shared_bound: This board uses a shared workflow
configuration.shared_bound_help: Changes to the shared definition apply here and to every other board using it. To change only this board, first make an independent copy.
configuration.shared_edit_help: Saving changes every board using this workflow. A state used by a task must keep its key and type. New rules apply to the next request.
configuration.shared_detach_help: Keep the current rules on this board. Later shared changes will no longer affect it.
configuration.shared_publish_help: Save this board's current rules as a shared workflow and use it here. You can then select it on another board you own.
configuration.shared_use: Use selected workflow on this board
configuration.shared_use_help: Replace this board's rules with the selected shared definition. Existing task states must remain valid. Later shared edits will apply to this board.
configuration.shared_empty: You have no shared workflows yet.
configuration.shared_delete_help: Delete this definition from your catalog. Its audit history remains available on the board that first shared it.

agents.title: AgentHub agents
agents.description: Register the agents that work in this environment. Each agent keeps the same identity across its keys and AI connections.
agents.empty: No agents are registered for this user yet.
agents.name: Display name
agents.id_help: Use a short name such as coding-agent. It cannot change after registration.
agents.roles_help: Choose the roles this agent needs. The environment owner controls agent permissions.
agents.wip_help: Leave blank for the environment default. Zero allows unlimited active tasks. The limit applies across projects.
agents.work_help: Only tasks you can access are listed here. The total includes all active work for this agent.
agents.owner_help: Only the environment owner changes permissions, limits and enabled state. You can rename agents assigned to you.
agents.key_help: Choose an agent to share its identity and task limit across credentials.
agents.choices_unavailable: Agent choices could not be loaded. Reload before making another key.
agents.oauth_help: Binding applies to every current and future sign-in for this user and the selected AI client, including refreshed sessions. Client names alone do not identify a connection.
agents.no_clients: Connect an AI client to this user first, then bind it here.
agents.kinds_help: One type per line. An empty list permits any valid type name.
agents.subject: Who this rule applies to
agents.subject_help: Use *, human, agent, role:name, kind:name or principal:identity.
agents.action_help: For example task.claim:ready or task.edit. Only * is a wildcard.
agents.selector_help: One value per line. Blank matches all projects or requires no labels.
agents.policy_help: The highest matching priority decides. A deny wins ties. Actions without a matching allow are refused.

access.title: Machine access
access.description: Review what an agent wants to do on your machines. Approval can be limited and revoked.
access.no_risks: No specific warnings were recorded. Review the scope before approving.
access.paths_help: Removing every path permits no paths. It never means unrestricted access. All other requested restrictions remain in place.
access.uses_help: Leave blank to keep the requested limit. Once permits one operation.
access.unsandboxed: Without a sandbox, a command may access everything available to the machine service account. Review the risk warnings carefully.
access.unchanged: Your change was not applied. Your draft is preserved below.
access.refused: Access change could not be completed
access.unavailable: Access records are temporarily unavailable. Keep your request and try again.
access.stale: This request changed or ended. Reload and review its current state before deciding.
access.request_count: {count} machine access requests need your review
access.no_scope: No additional restrictions were requested for this capability. Network and environment access still follow the grant rules.
